name: persuasion_v4
instructions: Below is a charity-donation chat: a persuader is trying to get the persuadee to donate to Save the Children. The text ends with 'Persuader message to tag:'. Classify ONLY that final persuader message (use earlier turns just for context): which persuasion strategy or dialogue act does it use? Choose by the function of the message, not just its wording.

criteria.greeting: Opening hello / hi / how are you today / good morning, or a simple greeting exchange such as 'I am well, how are you?'.
criteria.acknowledgement: A bare reaction or agreement token reacting to what the persuadee said, with no added content (answering a personal question about oneself, like 'I know I have', is 'other'): 'Great!', 'I agree', 'Yes', 'Me too', 'I understand', 'That sounds amazing', 'Absolutely', 'Ok'. NOT a compliment about the person (praise-user) and NOT gratitude (thank).
criteria.thank: Expresses gratitude: 'Thank you for helping', 'Thanks so much', 'We appreciate your help'.
criteria.praise-user: A compliment directed at the persuadee's character or generosity: 'That is very generous', 'You are a kind person'. Enthusiasm like a bare 'Great!' is acknowledgement, not praise.
criteria.proposition-of-donation: Asks or invites the person to donate at all (a yes/no decision), including declarative requests: 'Would you like to donate?', 'Would you consider donating to Save the Children?', 'Would you donate some of your payment?', 'Do you want to donate some too?', 'We are asking people today to give a small part of the payment for this HIT to the charity', 'I would appreciate it if some of the funds could be donated'.
criteria.ask-donation-amount: Asks HOW MUCH they will donate, or suggests/confirms a specific figure or percentage as the donation ask: 'How much would you like to give?', 'Say $500?', 'what percentage of your payment?', 'could you afford fifteen cents?', 'Would you prefer a one-time donation or monthly?'.
criteria.donation-information: Task mechanics about giving: how and where to donate, the payment deducted from the task payment, the allowed amount range ('You can choose any amount from $0 to all your payment'), URL or PayPal or credit-card details, that the money is sent to Save the Children, that donation is optional. NOT general statements about what the charity does with funds.
criteria.foot-in-the-door: Stresses that a small, tiny, any or little amount is enough, affordable or still helps, to make giving feel easy (the scaled-down ask): 'Even a small donation makes a big difference', 'Every little bit helps', 'Something as small as 5 cents could help', 'a tiny amount, even less than a dollar, can go a long way', 'only a small amount you would spend on coffee or snacks', 'Anything you can give is welcome', 'could you afford maybe fifteen cents?', 'you can do as little as 5 cents'.
criteria.logical-appeal: Explicit reasoning or evidence linking a donation to impact, or an argument rebutting the persuadee's objection: 'Your $1 pays for a child's school meals', 'economies of scale make your donation go further', 'scams do not stay around 100 years', 'if I could change a child's life and did not, I could not live with myself'. NOT plain descriptions of what the charity does or where it works (those are credibility-appeal or emotion-appeal), NOT general praise of the charity (other), and NOT statements that a small or any amount is enough (foot-in-the-door).
criteria.emotion-appeal: Stirs sympathy, empathy, guilt or feeling: vivid description of suffering or need, the persuader's own feelings about suffering or helplessness, imagining children in pain, appeals to compassion or gratitude for one's own good fortune. Examples: 'Millions of children in Syria face the daily threat of violence', 'These children die from hunger daily', 'think of all the kiddies you will be helping', 'I have a son and I cannot imagine him hungry or afraid', 'Every day I watch the news and feel powerless', 'Not everyone has it so it is good that you appreciate it', 'children are our future'. If a sentence mixes suffering with program facts, the sympathy-evoking content wins.
criteria.credibility-appeal: Facts about the organisation: what Save the Children is and does (its programs, where and how it works, sponsorships, funding), or its legitimacy, track record, ratings, finances, leaders, age. Also simply introducing the organisation. Examples: 'Save the Children was founded in 1919', 'They have programs for literacy and disaster relief', 'Through sponsorships and donations they are working to help children', 'Well I recently heard about Save the Children', 'rated highly by Charity Watch', 'only 5% goes to administration', 'the CEO is Carolyn Miles', 'we raised 2.5 million last year'. Stated as plain fact, without stirring feelings.
criteria.self-modeling: The persuader states a clear intention or act of donating or matching a donation, as a model for the persuadee: 'I am going to donate too', 'I gave what was given to me', 'I will donate 50% if you donate 30%'. General remarks about one's own habits in answer to a question ('I usually try to donate a little here and there', 'I know I have') are 'other'.
criteria.personal-story: A real narrative or anecdote about a specific experience or person tied to the cause or donating (not just a feeling or a general statement): 'I volunteer at a food bank; many families with young children come in', the story of Bruce, a child born to a teen mother, 'I have been to poor countries and saw...'.
criteria.source-related-inquiry: Asks whether the person knows or has heard of Save the Children, or what they know about the organisation: 'Have you heard of Save the Children?', 'what do you know about this organization?'.
criteria.task-related-inquiry: Asks the person's opinion, thoughts, concerns or questions about the charity, the task or the cause: 'What do you think?', 'Do you have any other questions?', 'what are your thoughts about child abuse?', 'do you want some info?', 'What are you not sure about?', 'what is the best way to help the kids?'.
criteria.personal-related-inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's own life or habits relevant to charity: 'do you donate to charities?', 'do you volunteer?', 'Do you have children?', 'Have you ever donated and been proud?'. 'How are you?' is greeting instead.
criteria.off-task: Genuinely unrelated chit-chat that has nothing to do with the donation task (weather, personal tangents, jokes). Closings like 'have a great night' are 'other', not off-task.
criteria.other: Anything that fits no other class: closing/goodbye remarks ('it was lovely chatting', 'have a great night'), rhetorical openers ('What if I told you that you can change the world?', 'Would you take it?'), the persuader answering a persuadee's question with substantive info about themself (own habits, job), plain self-disclosure, task logistics, unclear fragments, statements that are not any appeal.
